primitives.name: Captain Selection Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The captain should have sole power to select his team.
primitives.assumptions: The captain has complete information about player capabilities and team composition.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the captain's authority is undermined by external committees, team cohesion degrades.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Team composition as a constrained optimization problem. GSE: Situational adaptation through dynamic role assignment.
layer2.telemetry: Measurable metrics include team performance variance, decision-making speed, and post-game cohesion surveys.

primitives.name: Team Adaptation Based on Capabilities
primitives.verbatim_quote: One of the great secrets of good team play lies in adapting each play most carefully to the men taking part in it.
primitives.assumptions: Player strengths and weaknesses are known and measurable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misalignment between player roles and their inherent capabilities leads to inefficiency.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Player-specific tactical assignments maximize expected utility. GSE: State-transition matrices adjust based on real-time player performance.
layer2.telemetry: Track metrics such as play success rates, injury incidence, and individual contribution variance.

primitives.name: Self-Reliance in Emergencies
primitives.verbatim_quote: He should be a masterful man, and so self-reliant in emergencies that his men will naturally stand by him and look to him for advice, help, and commands.
primitives.assumptions: Emergencies are rare events with high stakes and limited information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Over-reliance on pre-planned protocols collapses under unprecedented circumstances.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Robust decision-making under uncertainty using conformal prediction intervals. GSE: Adaptive state transitions driven by leader intuition during critical junctures.
layer2.telemetry: Record emergency response times, decision accuracy, and team trust indicators.

primitives.name: Post-Play Debriefing
primitives.verbatim_quote: His relations with his men should, however, be such that he is always ready to listen to suggestions,—never, or very seldom, on the field, but after the play is over.
primitives.assumptions: Feedback loops are essential for continuous improvement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Lack of structured feedback results in stagnation and repeated errors.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Bayesian updating of player ratings based on peer and coach feedback. GSE: Iterative refinement of action-value functions via replay analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Monitor improvements in subsequent game performance and reduction in avoidable mistakes.

This maps directly to GSI's Bayesian network models for player valuation and GSE's Markov decision processes for game-state transitions. Failure occurs when this balance breaks, leading to either autocratic rigidity or chaotic disorganization. Historical precursors include von Neumann's minimax theorem and Shannon's communication theory, both emphasizing optimal strategies under imperfect information. Opposing agents (opponent captains) exploit asymmetries in information access and decision latency. Anti-collinearity conditions require ensuring that player attributes are linearly independent to prevent redundancy, while leakage vetoes involve protecting sensitive tactical data from being inferred by observing public behavior patterns.
